The relationship between voltage (V) and energy dissipation in a resistor is described by
Joule's law, which states that the power (P) dissipated as heat in a resistor is
proportional to the square of the voltage across it, given by the equation P = V^2/R,
where R is the resistance. If the voltage across the resistor is doubled, the new power
dissipation becomes P' = (2 V)^2/R = 4 V^2/R, indicating that the rate of energy
dissipation quadruples. Thus, if the original power dissipation was 2 W, it would increase
to 8 W when the voltage is doubled. This analysis highlights the quadratic relationship
between voltage and energy dissipation, emphasizing the significant impact of voltage
changes on power outputs in resistive components.
answers.explanation: The answer correctly identifies that power dissipation in a resistor is proportional to the square of the voltage across it, demonstrating that doubling the voltage leads to a quadrupling of the power dissipation due to the relationship expressed in Joule's law, P = V²/R.

The time period of each oscillation of an ultrasonic transducer operating at 6.7 MHz can
be calculated using the formula T = 1/f, where T is the time period and f is the
frequency. Substituting the given frequency, T = 1/(6.7 \times 10^6 Hz) results in
approximately 1.49 \times 10^-7 seconds, or 0.149 microseconds. To derive the angular
frequency (ω) in rad/s, we use the relationship ω = 2πf. Therefore, substituting the
frequency, ω = 2π(6.7 \times 10^6) gives an angular frequency of approximately 42,000
radians per second. This calculation highlights the inverse relationship between frequency
and time period, while also illustrating the conversion from frequency to angular
frequency in oscillatory systems.
